correctness.rationale: On compact support strictly inside the positive half-line, \(\log(X/K)\) and its square are bounded. Invariance of \(\log(X/K)\) gives \(\mathbb E[X]=K\). Invariance of its square and the exact increment r(1-X/K) gives \(2K\operatorname{Cov}(\log X,X)=r\operatorname{Var}(X)\). Positive variance yields the \(r\) formula; zero variance is exactly the fixed-point atom. The proof has explicit hypotheses and no finite-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: The precise invariant is motivated by structural parameter recovery in a canonical nonlinear population map. It gives a sharp dichotomy not supplied by the known periodic mean law: every non-equilibrium stationary one-time marginal identifies both \(K\) and \(r\), whereas the equilibrium marginal necessarily loses r. This is directly relevant to invariant-statistics interpretation and is not a renamed textbook first-moment calculation.
